text: The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran found that the government's repression of the 2022 'Woman, Life, Freedom' protests — unlawful killings, torture, rape, enforced disappearances and gender persecution — included serious violations amounting to crimes against humanity; it cited credible figures of up to 551 protesters killed, among them at least 49 women and 68 children.
short: UN Fact-Finding Mission: Iran's repression of the 2022 protests included crimes against humanity.

source.name: OHCHR: Iran: Institutional discrimination against women and girls enabled human rights violations and crimes against humanity in the context of recent protests, UN Fact-Finding Mission says (archived copy)
source.quote: serious human rights violations by the Government of Iran, many amounting to crimes against humanity
source.note: ohchr.org returned HTTP 403 to this script on 2026-10-01; the quote was verified on the Wayback Machine copy (capture 2026-09-19). The report details extra-judicial killings, arbitrary detention, torture, rape and enforced disappearances in the repression of the protests that began 16 September 2022.

additionalSources.name: The Guardian: UN: Iran committed crimes against humanity during protest crackdown
additionalSources.quote: The Iranian regime's human rights violations during its brutal suppression of protests in 2022 amount to crimes against humanity, a UN fact-finding mission (FFM) has said.
